extracted.intended_audience: typographers, book designers, printers, and press compositors
extracted.subtask_description: Printed specimen pages showing typefaces, point sizes, spacing treatments, and sample text used to evaluate appearance and legibility for book/press design. The page demonstrates multiple families (Monotype, Caslon Old Style), sizes, and setting variants (solid, leaded, gushing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Typeface family (MONOTYPE / CASLON OLD STYLE)
rubrics_metrics.description: The page identifies typeface families used for the specimens, e.g. 'MONOTYPE' and 'CASLON OLD STYLE'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specimens present the same text set in different type families to compare overall character, weight, and texture. Choose a family appropriate for the publication's tone and legibility; compare samples at intended reading sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point size (e.g., SIX POINT, SEVEN POINT, EIGHT POINT, NINE POINT, TEN POINT, ELEVEN POINT, TWELVE POINT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each specimen is headed by a point-size label (for example 'SIX POINT', 'EIGHT POINT', 'TEN POINT', 'TWELVE POINT'), showing how the same text reads at different sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use point-size specimens to assess legibility, line length, and optical color at reading distance. Select point size based on intended use (body text vs captions vs display).

rubrics_metrics.name: Type number / face number (e.g., NO. THIRTY-ONE, NO. EIGHT, NO. FIVE, NO. TWENTY-FIVE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens include a type or face number label such as 'NO. THIRTY-ONE' or 'NO. EIGHT' to identify the specific cut or design variant being shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Face numbers identify exact cuts/styles for ordering or comparison; verify the number when specifying type for composition or reprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting treatment: [Solid] vs [Leaded]
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens are marked '[Solid]' or '[Leaded]' indicating whether lines are set solid (no added leading) or with added leading (extra vertical space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare solid and leaded settings to judge readability, vertical rhythm, and overall page color; choose leaded for more open text color and improved legibility at small sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gushing variants (e.g., 'GUSHING' label in headings like 'SIX POINT GUSHING NO. TWENTY-FIVE')
rubrics_metrics.description: Some specimens are labeled with 'GUSHING' alongside point size and face number (e.g., 'SIX POINT GUSHING NO. TWENTY-FIVE'), indicating a specific casting/composition variant or treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gushing variants demonstrate alternate setting/ink/spread characteristics; examine these for how typeface behaves under different press or composition conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample text selection for evaluation ('When thoughtful Greeks like Polybius...')
rubrics_metrics.description: A long, representative paragraph (historical prose about Greeks, Alexander, Rome, etc.) is used repeatedly across specimens to show word spacing, hyphenation, and texture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use representative running text rather than isolated words to judge real-world readability, hyphenation behavior, ligatures, and overall color of set type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display of numerals and punctuation (rows like '1234567890' and symbol sequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens include sequences of numerals ('1234567890') and special symbol/glyph rows to show figure design and spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect numerals, punctuation, and special glyphs at intended sizes for uniform weight, alignment, and clarity, especially in tables or running figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uppercase/display lines and emphasis (ALL CAPS headings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Large uppercase lines (e.g., 'A WORLD-EMPIRE, INCLUDING ALL THE LANDS') are used to show display/headline behavior and emphasis in all-caps setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate caps for optical weight, tracking, and appropriateness for headlines or emphasis; observe how caps affect line breaks and page rhythm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration of vowel/glyph combinations and diacritics (aeiou sequences, 'AEIOU' rows)
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated vowel sequences and assorted small letter groupings appear to illustrate internal letter shapes, counters, and kerning behavior ('AEIOU', 'aeiou', varied sequences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use such sequences to assess internal color, x-height, and spacing relationships; helpful for judging readability and consistency across glyphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of leaded specimen notes (bracketed notes like '[Leaded]' and bracketed section headers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bracketed notes and headers are placed with specimens to indicate specific composition or treatment choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to these labels when comparing samples; they document the exact setting conditions used for each specimen.
